root_cause.text: IPVS checksum validation for IPv6 packets in the TCP/UDP/SCTP handlers assumed the transport header starts immediately after the fixed IPv6 header and used `ipv6_hdr(skb)->nexthdr`, so packets with IPv6 extension headers were parsed and checksummed at the wrong offset/protocol.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `tcp_csum_check`, `udp_csum_check`, and `sctp_csum_check` to receive the already computed transport-header offset (`tcphoff`/`udphoff`/`sctphoff`) instead of using `sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)`, and replaces IPv6 pseudo-header protocol selection from `ipv6_hdr(skb)->nexthdr` to fixed `IPPROTO_TCP`/`IPPROTO_UDP`; the commit message explicitly says “Protocol checksum validation fails for IPv6 if there are extension headers before the protocol header. iph->len already contains its offset, so use it to fix the problem.”

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
IPVS: Add 'af' args to protocol handler functions

Add 'af' arguments to conn_schedule(), conn_in_get(), conn_out_get()
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it directly shows the IPv6 checksum/parsing logic in question. The vulnerable construct is present in the IPv6 path: when `af == AF_INET6`, the code sets `tcphoff = sizeof(struct ipv6hdr);` (line 229), which assumes the transport header begins immediately after the fixed 40-byte IPv6 header. It then computes/verifies the checksum using `ipv6_hdr(skb)->nexthdr` as the upper-layer protocol in `csum_ipv6_magic(..., ipv6_hdr(skb)->nexthdr, skb->csum)` (lines 240-244). This matches the root cause exactly: packets with IPv6 extension headers will have the real transport header at a later offset, and `nexthdr` in the base IPv6 header may indicate an extension header rather than TCP/UDP/SCTP. There is no logic here to walk IPv6 extension headers or derive the correct transport offset/protocol, so the fix is not present.

Add 'af' arguments to conn_schedule(), conn_in_get(), conn_out_get()
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it directly shows the IPv6 checksum/parsing logic in question. The vulnerable construct is present. For IPv6, the code sets `udphoff = sizeof(struct ipv6hdr);` at line 245, which assumes the UDP header starts immediately after the fixed IPv6 header and does not account for IPv6 extension headers. It then reads the UDP header from that offset via `skb_header_pointer(skb, udphoff, sizeof(_udph), &_udph);` at line 250. In the checksum validation path, for IPv6 it uses `csum_ipv6_magic(..., skb->len - udphoff, ipv6_hdr(skb)->nexthdr, skb->csum)` at lines 262-266, which uses `ipv6_hdr(skb)->nexthdr` from the fixed IPv6 header rather than the actual transport protocol after extension headers. This exactly matches the root cause: checksum validation for IPv6 assumes no extension headers and uses the wrong offset/protocol. There is no visible fix here such as using the real transport header offset or the resolved next header after parsing extension headers, so `is_fixed` is false.

commit 2906f66a5682e5670a5eefe991843689b8d8563f
Author: Venkata Mohan Reddy <mohanreddykv@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Feb 18 12:31:05 2010 +0100

    ipvs: SCTP Trasport Loadbalancing Support
    
    Enhance IPVS to load balance SCTP transport protocol packets. This is done
    based on the SCTP rfc 4960. All possible control chunks have been taken
    care. The state machine used in this code looks some what lengthy. I tried
    to make the state machine easy to understand.
    
    Signed-off-by:
bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in this new SCTP protocol implementation, especially in `sctp_snat_handler`, `sctp_dnat_handler`, `sctp_csum_check`, and `set_sctp_state`. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is present: for IPv6, the code assumes the SCTP header begins immediately after the fixed IPv6 header. Specifically, in multiple places it does `if (af == AF_INET6) sctphoff = sizeof(struct ipv6hdr);` (or `if (cp->af == AF_INET6) sctphoff = sizeof(struct ipv6hdr);`) and otherwise uses `ip_hdrlen(skb)`. This appears in `sctp_snat_handler`, `sctp_dnat_handler`, and `sctp_csum_check`. That means any IPv6 extension headers are ignored and parsing/checksuming occurs at the wrong offset. Likewise, `set_sctp_state` uses `ihl = cp->af == AF_INET ? ip_hdrlen(skb) : sizeof(struct ipv6hdr);` and then reads the SCTP chunk header at `ihl + sizeof(sctp_sctphdr_t)`, again assuming no IPv6 extension headers. There is no logic here to walk IPv6 extension headers or use a precomputed transport-header offset/protocol derived from proper IPv6 parsing. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not present.
